name: Kaguya (SELENE)
payload: 3020 kg launch mass; 2914 kg main orbiter; two 53 kg subsatellites (Okina, Ouna)
first: High-definition video of Earth rising over the Moon's limb
description: Kaguya, formally SELENE (Selenological and Engineering Explorer), was Japan's second lunar orbiter after Hiten. Launched on an H-IIA from Tanegashima on 2007-09-14, it carried a 2914 kg main orbiter and two 53 kg subsatellites, Okina and Ouna. All three names come from The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter, whose heroine, Kaguya, is a princess from the Moon. Okina relayed the orbiter's radio link from behind the Moon, which allowed Doppler tracking of the far side's gravity, and Ouna served as a radio source for VLBI tracking. After lunar orbit insertion on 2007-10-03 the orbiter settled into a circular polar orbit at 100 km on 2007-10-18 (Japan time). There its terrain camera, multiband imager, spectral profiler, X-ray and gamma-ray spectrometers, laser altimeter and radar sounder mapped the Moon's shape, composition, gravity and magnetism, while its high-definition camera filmed Earth rising over the limb. The orbiter was lowered to about 50 km on 2009-02-01 and, on 2009-06-10, commanded into a controlled impact near Gill crater.

events.label: LOI
events.note: Lunar orbit insertion 2007-10-03 into a polar orbit with a 100 km perilune.

events.label: OKINA RELEASED
events.note: The relay satellite is released 2007-10-09 into a 100 x 2400 km orbit.

events.label: OUNA RELEASED
events.note: The VLBI radio-source satellite is released 2007-10-12 into a 100 x 800 km orbit.

events.label: 100 KM ORBIT
events.note: Circular polar orbit at 100 km reached 2007-10-18 (Japan time); the main science phase begins.

events.label: OKINA IMPACT
events.note: Okina falls on the far side near Mineur D crater 2009-02-12.

events.label: CONTROLLED IMPACT
events.note: The main orbiter is commanded into the surface near Gill crater 2009-06-10 18:25 UTC, ending the mission.
